issues.legal_issue: A rule-making power to provide for supervision over member institutions does not authorize the supervisory body to create a centralized cadre of their employees or make them employees of that body.
material_facts: A rule authorized the central body to create a centralized service for employees of member mortgage banks, appoint employees to posts in that service, and deprive the member banks of appointment powers over those posts.
The rule also required member banks to contribute to the cost of the service and vested employees’ service rights, privileges, and liabilities in the central body.

The governing Act gave the central body supervisory powers over member banks, including specified powers concerning their employees, while separately empowering the Registrar to create a common cadre for a class of societies.
issues.conclusion: The rule exceeded the authority conferred by the Act and was ultra vires.
issues.legal_principle: The rule-making power under section 130(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Co-operative Societies Act, 1964, is confined to purposes enumerated or indicated in the Act. Section 115 gives the Board supervisory power over mortgage banks, including specified powers concerning their employees, but does not authorize the Board to create a centralized cadre or recruit for it. Section 116A separately empowers the Registrar to create a common cadre for a class of societies and to require contributions toward its cost. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.delegated_rule_validity_challenge: A party challenged the validity of a rule made under delegated authority.
predicates.governing_law_confines_supervision_to_me: The governing law gives a supervisory body powers over member institutions and their employees but does not give it authority to create a centralized cadre for those employees.
predicates.supervisory_body_creates_centralized_ser: The supervisory body made a rule creating a centralized service for employees of member institutions and assigning employment powers to itself.

issues.definition: When a challenged delegated rule creates a centralized service for member institutions’ employees beyond the supervisory authority provided by the governing law, the rule is ultra vires.

issues.legal_issue: A supervisory power concerning transfers of employees does not authorize transferring an employee between distinct member institutions so as to change the employee’s employer.
material_facts: The Act provided for supervision over mortgage banks, including a power concerning transfers of their employees.
The challenged rule established a centralized service that could result in employees being moved between separate mortgage banks.
The Court considered the Act’s reference to employees of the mortgage banks and the provision in model bye-laws for recording transfers within a bank.
issues.conclusion: The transfer power is confined to transfers between branches of the same mortgage bank and does not include transfers between separate mortgage banks.
issues.legal_principle: Section 115 of the Andhra Pradesh Co-operative Societies Act, 1964, places the power concerning transfers within a supervisory framework over employees of mortgage banks. The word “transfer” does not authorize changing the employer by moving an employee from one mortgage bank to another; it refers to movement between branches of the same bank. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.delegated_rule_validity_challenge: A party challenged the validity of a rule governing employment arrangements under delegated authority.
predicates.supervisory_transfer_power_concerns_memb: The governing law gives a supervisory body a power concerning transfers of employees of member institutions.
predicates.proposed_transfer_changes_employee_to_a_: The employment arrangement provides for an employee to move from one member institution to another, thereby changing the employer.

issues.definition: If a transfer under a supervisory power would change an employee’s employer, the power covers only transfers between branches of the same employer.

issues.legal_issue: A central funding institution does not acquire authority to collect loans made by member institutions, or a right to payment from their borrowers, merely because it funds those institutions or holds transferred security.
material_facts: Mortgage banks advanced loans to borrowers, and the Act assigned the recovery of those loans to the mortgage banks.

The central mortgage bank provided funds to the member mortgage banks, and security associated with loans made by mortgage banks was deemed transferred to the central bank to secure the central bank’s advances.
The Act did not create a direct contractual liability between borrowers and the central mortgage bank; amounts due on the borrowers’ loans remained payable to the mortgage banks that made them.
issues.conclusion: The central mortgage bank had no authority under the Act to collect loans advanced by member mortgage banks, and borrowers owed repayment to the mortgage banks that advanced the loans, not to the central mortgage bank.
issues.legal_principle: The provisions of the Andhra Pradesh Co-operative Societies Act, 1964, governing recovery place collection of loans on the mortgage bank that advanced them. The deemed transfer of security under section 94 secures the central mortgage bank’s advances to member banks, while section 95 preserves payment of amounts due to the mortgage bank. In the absence of a provision creating direct contractual liability to the central mortgage bank, the borrower’s liability is to the lending mortgage bank. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.member_institution_advanced_loan_to_borr: A member institution advanced a loan directly to a borrower.
predicates.central_body_funded_member_institution: A central body provided funding to the member institution.
predicates.security_was_transferred_to_secure_centr: Security associated with the member institution’s lending was transferred to the central body to secure the central body’s advances to the member institution.
predicates.no_direct_borrower_liability_to_central_: The governing arrangement did not make the borrower directly liable to repay the central body.

issues.definition: When a member institution lends to a borrower and the central body’s funding and security arrangements do not make the borrower directly liable to it, repayment is owed only to the lending institution.
